newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan 1995/96 c/a gap swells to 6.6 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan 1995/96 c/a gap swells to 6.6 pct of GDP.

text.p: Pakistan's current account deficit widened to 6.6 percent of gross domestic product in 1995/96 from 3.6 percent in 1994/95, the central bank said in its annual report released on Thursday.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said the current account gap, which the government had aimed to reduce to 4.4 percent of GDP, had worsened because exports had grown only seven percent, while imports expanded 16.2 percent and workers' remittances declined 21 percent.

"However, the almost tripling of foreign direct investment to $1.1 billion and a sizeable increase in foreign currency deposits helped mitigate the impact of the wider current account deficit," the bank said.
It said foreign reserves stood at $2.1 billion at the end of 1995/96. Foreign reserves, including gold and special drawing rights, currently stand at $1.45 billion, SBP figures show.
